root_idea.summary: The root centers on opening or initiating something, putting it first, and bringing it into existence.
root_idea.development: From the basic idea of opening or beginning, the lexical development extends to giving precedence, originating or creating anew, first occurrence, first place, and related nouns for beginnings and principles.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb with distinct senses of beginning with, commencing, and originating.
Quran-attested Form IV verb meaning to originate or bring forth in the first instance.

senses.definition: To begin with something; put it first or give it precedence; in a hostile context, to initiate the action against someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with بِـ for beginning with or giving precedence to something; it may also describe being the party that initiates an action.

senses.definition: To begin or commence an action, affair, or sequence.
senses.usage_conditions: Describes the start of an activity or ordered course, without necessarily implying creation of the thing begun.

senses.definition: To originate, create, or bring into existence for the first time.
senses.usage_conditions: Used especially of bringing creation or a created order into existence, and of an origin that has no preceding instance.

senses.definition: To originate or produce something in the first instance; bring it forth as new.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative form used for origination or production, including divine origination; it emphasizes bringing something into being rather than merely starting an activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act or state of beginning; a commencement. In expressions of return, the beginning may be the point to which one returns or from which one recommences.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun and noun of beginning, including idioms for doing something again from its starting point.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first or former thing, preceding all others; also a first thought, opinion, or impression formed before fuller consideration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions meaning at first, as a first matter, or at the first appearance of an opinion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chief or lord occupying the first place in chieftainship; by extension, an intelligent or capable young man whose judgment is consulted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A social-status and leadership use, with plural بُدُوءٌ reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A share or portion of a slaughtered camel, especially a best portion; also a joint or a bone with its meat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical term for portions distributed from a slaughtered camel, including portions associated with the game of maysir.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dig a well for the first time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive use referring to the initial digging of a well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go forth from one land to another, or from one's own land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with مِنْ to mark the land from which one departs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be afflicted with smallpox, measles, or a similar eruptive illness; more generally, to fall sick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-form expression for being attacked by illness, including inquiry about when a person became ill.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do or produce a new, previously unknown, strange, or wonderful thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Form IV extension emphasizing novelty or unfamiliarity rather than the Quranic creation sense alone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To void excrement or break wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic bodily use of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put forth one's second teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a child or a colt during the replacement of its first teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To begin or make a beginning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived Form V expression for entering upon a beginning; it is not a separate Quran-attested form group in this packet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone a promise in anticipation, without that person first asking for it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction اِبْتَدَأَهُ بِوَعْدٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The beginning or outward course of a military expedition, as opposed to its return course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized military term contrasted with رَجْعَةٌ, the homeward course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first period of one's condition or life, especially one's youth or adolescence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions referring to the beginning of a person's state or development.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain black plant resembling a truffle and regarded as useless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical lexical item distinct from the noun for a beginning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Excrement from the anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive associated with the bodily use of أَبْدَأَ; it is kept distinct from that verb's headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Originated or newly brought into existence; unprecedented, strange, or wonderful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a thing not previously existing or not made after the likeness of an earlier thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A newly dug well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical description of a well dug recently or in previously unoccupied ground, contrasted with an ancient or pre-existing well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first occurrence of something, especially an occurrence that happens unexpectedly or takes one unawares.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May also denote the first of anything; plural بَدَايَا is reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The faculty of extemporizing or producing speech and accounts through prompt intelligence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's quickness and ability to utter or relate things spontaneously.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or time at which something begins; a starting point.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Originally a noun of place or time derived from the verb of beginning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A principle or first rule of a science or other system.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often used in the plural مَبَادِئُ for foundational principles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The primary or initial import of a word, opposed to its ultimate or extended end.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical metalinguistic use contrasted with غَايَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Creator or Originator who produced existing things at the beginning, not after the likeness of anything pre-existing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A divine epithet and participial title, distinct in headword from the Quran-attested finite Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man experienced through repeated war or raiding expeditions; also a horse repeatedly trained and exercised and therefore obedient to its rider.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the compound مُبْدِئٌ مُعِيدٌ for repeated experience and practiced ability.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Passive participle gloss without an independent lexical branch.

cautions: Lane's discussion of بَادِئَ/بَادِيَ الرَّأْيِ involves variant Quran readings and is retained as broader lexical evidence, not assigned to a QAC Quran form because no corresponding form group is supplied here.
Lane's printed citation for the expression involving يُبْدِئُ uses its historical citation notation; the modern Form IV examples use only the independently supplied QAC locations 34:49 and 85:13.
